title: The Three Little Birds variant

full_text:
Three sisters were tending sheep near the royal meadows when the king rode by. The eldest said, "If I marry the king, I will spin him the finest shirts." The second said, "If I marry the king, I will bake him bread sweeter than honey." But the youngest whispered, "If I marry the king, I will bear him three golden-haired children who weep pearls and laugh roses."

The king chose the youngest sister and married her in great joy. But her envious older sisters conspired with the wicked queen-mother. Whenever the young queen gave birth—first to two brave boys and then to a lovely girl, each with a golden star upon their brows—the sisters stole the babies away, threw them into the rushing river, and placed whimpering puppies in their cradles, driving the king to banish his heartbroken wife to a stone tower.

Providence watched over the children. A kindly fisherman drew them from the water in his net, raised them as his own, and taught them gentle manners. When the siblings grew up, they journeyed to find the magical singing bird, the golden water, and the dancing tree that could restore their royal heritage.

Guided by their pure hearts, the siblings broke the mountain enchantment and captured the miraculous speaking bird. Brought before the king at a great royal banquet, the bird sang the true tale of the discarded babies, the wicked aunt's deceit, and the innocent queen weeping in her tower.

Overwhelmed with remorse and joy, the king embraced his three golden-starred children, released his faithful queen from her tower, and banished the envious sisters forever, filling the royal realm with long-lost laughter and song.
moral: Innocent children protected by providence cannot be destroyed by wicked slander.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Three Little Birds variant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
